definition_en: a person who has broken the law, or connected with crime
core_image: 一个人戴着手铐被带进法庭，旁听席立刻安静
scene: 法警押着一个人走进法庭，旁听席立刻安静下来。The criminal kept his eyes on the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 criminal 指「罪犯」（第 1 个义项：犯了法的人）；句意是那名罪犯一直盯着地面。

senses.title: A person who breaks the law
senses.definition: a person who has committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 已经犯了罪的人
senses.example: The criminal was caught at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 那名罪犯在边境被抓。
senses.why: One act is enough to give a person the name.
senses.whyCN: 一桩行为，就足以给一个人安上这个名字。

senses.title: Connected with crime
senses.definition: relating to crime or to its punishment
senses.definitionCN: 与罪行或对其惩罚有关的
senses.example: He now faces criminal charges.
senses.exampleCN: 他现在面临刑事指控。
senses.why: A whole branch of law is named after the act it handles.
senses.whyCN: 法律的一整支，是用它处理的行为来命名的。

senses.title: Seriously wrong
senses.definition: seriously wrong or shameful, though not against the law
senses.definitionCN: 严重错误或可耻，但并不违法
senses.example: It is criminal to leave a child alone.
senses.exampleCN: 把小孩独自丢下简直不可原谅。
senses.why: The court of the heart also uses this word.
senses.whyCN: 心里的那个法庭，也会用这个词。

intro.en: Criminal comes from Latin criminalis, from crimen, a charge, through Old French.
intro.cn: criminal 源自拉丁语 criminalis，再往上是 crimen（指控），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Crimen meant a charge brought against a person.
items.cn: crimen 指对一个人提出的指控。

items.en: Criminalis described what belonged to such a charge.
items.cn: criminalis 形容与这类指控相关的事物。

items.en: Criminel named a person accused of a wrong.
items.cn: criminel 指被控做错事的人。

items.en: Criminal named both the person and the act.
items.cn: criminal 既指人，也指行为。

items.en: Criminal law grew into a branch of its own.
items.cn: 刑法长成了独立的一支。

items.en: It can also scold a shameful act that no law covers.
items.cn: 它也能用来斥责法律管不到的可耻行为。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crim- stem, and the meaning group names people caught up in a case.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crim- 词干，近义组列出案件里被牵涉的几种人。

entries.definition: an act that breaks the law
the study of crime and its causes
entries.definitionCN: 研究犯罪及其成因的学科

entries.definition: to suggest that someone is guilty
a person who breaks a rule or law
a person thought to have done wrong
a person found guilty in court
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上被判有罪的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a courtroom door to a careless act at home.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从法庭的门，跑到家里一桩粗心的行为。

normal.en: Criminal is crime plus -inal: a person made of one act.
normal.cn: criminal 是 crime 加 -inal：由一桩行为做成的人。

normal.en: Handcuffs write the first line of the story.
normal.cn: 手铐写下了这个故事的第一行。

normal.en: A record keeps the past standing in the present.
normal.cn: 一份记录让过去站在现在里。

normal.en: The word fits both the man and the law that chases him.
normal.cn: 这个词既合那个人，也合追他的那部法。

normal.en: When no law applies, the heart still says criminal.
normal.cn: 法律管不到时，心仍会说一句可耻。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow in a police photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象警局照片里的一个黑影。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp on a thick file.
abstract.cn: 想象一份厚档案上的一枚印章。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door with a child behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门锁着，门后有个孩子。

examples.en: The criminal gave himself up at dawn.
examples.cn: 那名罪犯在黎明自首了。

examples.en: She has no criminal record.
examples.cn: 她没有犯罪记录。

examples.en: Wasting a whole day would be criminal.
examples.cn: 浪费一整天简直不可原谅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 criminal 记成 crime（罪行）加 -inal：做下那桩罪行的人，就是罪犯。

root: 源自拉丁语 crimen（指控）与 criminalis（与指控有关的）；本义是「被控有罪的人」，后兼指犯罪的、刑事的，也可引申为道德上可耻的。

sensesIntro.en: From the person charged, to the law that tries him, to the moral verdict on a shameful act.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被控的人，到审他的那部法，再到对可耻行为的道德判决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handcuffed man walking into a quiet court.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个戴手铐的人走进安静的法庭。

branches.en: The person who did the act carries the name.
branches.cn: 做了那件事的人，就带着这个名字。

branches.en: The law itself takes the same adjective.
branches.cn: 法律本身也用同一个形容词。

branches.en: Shame can use the word where no court can.
branches.cn: 法庭到不了的地方，羞耻可以用这个词。

branches.en: A criminal is judged by criminal law.
branches.cn: 罪犯由刑法来审判。

branches.en: Both meanings condemn, one in court and one in the heart.
branches.cn: 两个意思都在谴责，一个在法庭，一个在心里。

intro.en: Criminal adds -inal to the Latin stem crim-, the same stem as crime.
intro.cn: criminal 在拉丁词干 crim- 后加 -inal，与 crime 同干。

latinIntro.en: Latin crimen, a charge, gives criminal, criminology and incriminate alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crimen（指控）同时生出 criminal、criminology 与 incriminate。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the law
items.exampleCN: 那名罪犯一言不发地站着。
这笔钱是以犯罪手段取得的。
犯罪学解释盗窃的规律。

items.example: The report measured criminality by district.
items.exampleCN: 报告按区衡量了犯罪状况。
这盘录音使两名男子显得有罪。

items.meaning: a charge made back at an accuser
items.meaningCN: 反过来对指控者的指责

items.meaning: to remove the criminal status of something
items.example: They voted to decriminalize the offence.
items.exampleCN: 他们投票把这一行为除罪化。

definition_en: a time of great danger or difficulty that must be dealt with at once
core_image: 水位不断上涨，堤坝上的人只剩几个小时做决定
scene: 河水快漫过堤顶，所有人都在等一个决定。The flood brought the town to a crisis.
sceneCN: 这里 crisis 指「危机」（第 1 个义项：必须立即应对的危险时刻）；句意是洪水把小镇推到了危机之中。

senses.title: A time of great danger
senses.definition: a moment of great danger when a decision must be made quickly
senses.definitionCN: 必须迅速做出决定的极度危险的时刻
senses.example: The country faced a serious economic crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家面临严重的经济危机。
senses.why: Danger that waits becomes damage that cannot be undone.
senses.whyCN: 拖延的危险，会变成无法挽回的损失。

senses.title: The turning point
senses.definition: the point in an illness or a story where things must turn better or worse
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或事情发展到必须转好或转坏的关头
senses.example: The fever reached its crisis on the third night.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧在第三天夜里到了紧要关头。
senses.why: An illness also arrives at a fork and must choose a side.
senses.whyCN: 疾病也会走到一个岔口，必须选一边。

senses.title: A lasting hard state
senses.definition: a continuing state of serious difficulty in a society or system
senses.definitionCN: 社会或系统中持续存在的严重困难状态
senses.example: The housing crisis has lasted for years.
senses.exampleCN: 住房困境已经持续多年。
senses.why: Some turning points never quite turn, and become everyday life.
senses.whyCN: 有些转折点始终没转过去，就成了日常。

intro.en: Crisis comes from Greek krisis, a decision, from krinein, to separate or judge.
intro.cn: crisis 源自希腊语 krisis（决断），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开或判断。

items.en: Krisis named a decision or a turning point.
items.cn: krisis 指决断或转折点。

items.en: Medical Latin used crisis for the decisive point of an illness.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 crisis 指疾病的决定性时刻。

items.en: Crisis entered English first as a medical term.
items.cn: crisis 最初作为医学术语进入英语。

items.en: It spread to politics, money and daily life.
items.cn: 它扩展到政治、金钱与日常生活。

items.en: It now names any dangerous turning point.
items.cn: 今天它指任何危险的转折点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cri- stem of judging, and the meaning group names other moments of danger.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示判断的 cri- 词干，近义组列出其他危险的时刻。

entries.definition: a person who judges works or actions

entries.definitionCN: 非常严重或非常关键的

entries.definition: words that judge faults or merits
a sudden dangerous event needing quick action
entries.definitionCN: 需要迅速行动的突发危险事件

entries.definition: a particular point in time or events
entries.definitionCN: 时间或事件中的某个特定节点

entries.definition: a difficult situation hard to escape

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with rising water and end with a fork that never closes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从上涨的水开始，最后落到一个始终没合上的岔口。

normal.en: Crisis and critic share a root: both are about judging.
normal.cn: crisis 与 critic 同根：两者都关乎判断。

normal.en: A crisis is a clock with no spare hours.
normal.cn: 危机是一只没有多余时辰的钟。

normal.en: Two roads open, and neither waits.
normal.cn: 两条路一起打开，谁也不等你。

normal.en: The word sounds like cry, and someone always cries.
normal.cn: 这个词听着像 cry，而总有人在哭。

normal.en: A long crisis is just a turn that never came.
normal.cn: 漫长的危机，只是一个始终没来的转折。

abstract.en: Picture water an inch below the top of a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象水面离墙顶只差一寸。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone looks at one clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人都盯着同一只钟。

abstract.en: Picture a road split with no sign at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成两岔，却没有路牌。

examples.en: The government acted quickly during the crisis.
examples.cn: 政府在危机期间行动迅速。

examples.en: Two crises hit the company in one year.
examples.cn: 一年之内两场危机击中了这家公司。

examples.en: The illness passed its crisis before dawn.
examples.cn: 病情在天亮前过了危险期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crisis 记成一个必须当场做决定的岔路口：一步走错，后面全变，这就是危机。

root: 源自希腊语 krisis（决断、判断），再往上是 krinein（分开、辨别）；本义是「必须做出决断的那一刻」，由医学上的危险期扩展到政治、经济与生活的转折关头。

sensesIntro.en: From a dangerous moment that demands a decision, to a turning point, to a difficulty that never turns.
sensesIntro.cn: 从必须决断的危险时刻，到转折点，再到始终没转过去的困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water rising to the top of a dike.
core.cn: 核心意象：水涨到堤坝顶端。

branches.en: Danger grows until a decision can no longer wait.
branches.cn: 危险渐长，直到决断再也不能等。

branches.en: An illness or a story reaches a fork and turns.
branches.cn: 疾病或事情走到岔口，然后转向。

branches.en: When the turn never comes, difficulty becomes normal.
branches.cn: 转折没来时，困难就成了常态。

branches.en: Every crisis is a decision point under pressure.
branches.cn: 每一场危机都是压力下的决断点。

branches.en: Some turning points last so long that they turn into daily life.
branches.cn: 有些转折拖得太久，就变成了日常。

intro.en: Crisis belongs to the Greek family of krinein, to judge, which also gives critic and criterion.
intro.cn: crisis 属于希腊语 krinein（判断）这一族，critic 与 criterion 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Greek stem kri- passed into Latin and English as cri-, the stem of judging.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词干 kri- 经拉丁语进入英语，变成表示判断的 cri-。

items.exampleCN: 这场危机考验了每一位领导者。

items.meaningCN: 非常严重或非常关键的
items.exampleCN: 接下来的一小时至关重要。

items.example: The critic praised the new play.
items.exampleCN: 评论家称赞了这部新戏。
这项计划招来尖锐批评。

items.example: They criticize the choice of site.

items.meaning: a careful judgement of a work
in a way that decides the outcome

definition_zh: 脆的；清爽的；干脆的；薯片
definition_en: firm and dry enough to break with a sharp sound, or clear and fresh
core_image: 一掰苹果，清脆的一声在空气里炸开
scene: 她咬下一口苹果，清脆的一声在安静的厨房里响起。The apple was cool and crisp.
sceneCN: 这里 crisp 指「脆的」（第 1 个义项：坚实干燥、咬断时发出清脆声响的）；句意是那只苹果又凉又脆。

senses.title: Firm and breaking sharply
senses.definition: firm and dry enough to break with a sharp sound
senses.definitionCN: 坚实干燥，断时会发出清脆声响
senses.example: The bread was still warm and crisp.
senses.exampleCN: 面包还热着，而且很脆。
senses.why: Dry fibres snap instead of bending, and the ear hears it.
senses.whyCN: 干燥的纤维不弯而断，耳朵立刻听见。

senses.title: Cool, dry and clear
senses.definition: of air or weather, cool, dry and clear
senses.definitionCN: 指空气或天气凉爽、干燥而清澈
senses.example: A crisp morning wind came off the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵清爽的晨风从海上吹来。
senses.why: Cold dry air feels as clean as a snapped twig sounds.
senses.whyCN: 干冷的空气，听上去就像折断一根细枝那样干净。

senses.title: Brief and direct
senses.definition: of speech or manner, brief, clear and direct
senses.definitionCN: 指言语或举止简短、清楚而直接
senses.example: Her answer was short and crisp.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答简短而干脆。
senses.why: A sentence can also break cleanly, with no soft edges.
senses.whyCN: 一句话也能断得干净，没有拖泥带水。

intro.en: Crisp comes from Latin crispus, curled, which entered English from Old English crisp.
intro.cn: crisp 源自拉丁语 crispus（卷曲的），经古英语 crisp 进入现代英语。

items.en: Crispus meant curled or wavy.
items.cn: crispus 意为卷曲的、有波纹的。

items.en: Crisp first described curled hair.
items.cn: crisp 最初形容卷曲的头发。

items.en: It moved to things that break with a sharp sound.
items.cn: 它转指断时发出清脆声响的东西。

items.en: It described fresh, bracing air.
items.cn: 它用来形容清新提神的空气。

items.en: It named thin fried slices of potato.
items.cn: 它指切得很薄油炸的土豆片。

items.en: It also means brief and direct in speech.
items.cn: 它也表示言语简短直接。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crisp stem, and the meaning group names other sharp or fresh qualities.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crisp 词干，近义组列出其他清脆或清新的性质。

entries.definition: in a brief and clear way

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a snapped twig and end with a short answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一根折断的细枝开始，最后落到一句简短的回答。

normal.en: Crisp sounds like a bite: one clean crack.
normal.cn: crisp 听起来就是一口咬下：一声干脆的裂响。

normal.en: Thin ice, dry leaves, cold apples all say crisp.
normal.cn: 薄冰、干叶、冷苹果，都会说一声清脆。

normal.en: Cold air and a short answer share the same edge.
normal.cn: 冷空气和短回答，边缘是一样的锋利。

normal.en: If it does not bend, it may crisply break.
normal.cn: 不肯弯的东西，往往会清脆地断。

normal.en: A crisp morning wakes you faster than coffee.
normal.cn: 清爽的早晨比咖啡更快叫醒你。

abstract.en: Picture a dry leaf breaking under a shoe.
abstract.cn: 想象一片干叶在鞋底下碎裂。

abstract.en: Picture breath turning white in cold air.
abstract.cn: 想象冷空气里呼出的白气。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence cut off with a full stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被一个句号干净地截住。

examples.en: The toast stayed crisp under the eggs.
examples.cn: 吐司在鸡蛋下面还是脆的。

examples.en: The air was crisp and full of autumn light.
examples.cn: 空气清爽，满是秋日的光。

examples.en: He gave a crisp answer and left.
examples.cn: 他干脆地答了一句就走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crisp 记成咬苹果那一声脆响：又干又硬，一咬就断，清脆利落。

root: 源自拉丁语 crispus（卷曲的），经古英语 crisp 而来；本义形容卷发，后转指干燥易断、发出脆响之物，再引申为空气清爽与言语干脆。

sensesIntro.en: From a clean snap, to clean air, to a clean sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一声清脆的断响，到清爽的空气，再到一句干净的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an apple breaking with a sharp crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只苹果被咬开时清脆的一响。

branches.en: Dry and firm things break with a clean sound.
branches.cn: 干燥坚实的东西断得干净利落。

branches.en: Cold dry air carries the same clean edge.
branches.cn: 干冷的空气带着同样的清爽边缘。

branches.en: Speech can be as short and clean as a snap.
branches.cn: 说话也能像断响一样短而干净。

branches.en: Both an apple and a morning can wake the senses.
branches.cn: 苹果和早晨都能叫醒感官。

branches.en: Crisp air and crisp words both refuse to be soft.
branches.cn: 清爽的空气和干脆的话，都不肯软下来。

intro.en: Crisp is an old word that now builds a small family of adjectives, adverbs and nouns.
intro.cn: crisp 是个老词，如今长出一小族形容词、副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crispus, curled, is the distant source of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crispus（卷曲的）是这一整族词的远源。

items.example: She spoke crisply into the phone.
The crispness of the air surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 空气的清爽让我们意外。

items.example: He opened a bag of crisps.
The cold crisped the fallen leaves.
A little fat helps the crisping.

items.meaning: a thin dry biscuit of rye

definition_en: a standard by which something is judged or decided
core_image: 评委桌上摊着一张打分表，一条条标准逐项勾选
scene: 评委把打分表铺在桌上，一行行对照。Cost was not the only criterion for the choice.
sceneCN: 这里 criterion 指「标准」（第 1 个义项：用来评判或决定事物的依据）；句意是成本并不是这次选择的唯一标准。

senses.title: A standard for judging
senses.definition: a standard by which something is judged or decided
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判或决定某事物的标准
senses.example: Safety is our first criterion.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们的第一标准。
senses.why: To choose one thing you must first know what counts.
senses.whyCN: 要挑出一样东西，先得知道什么才算数。

senses.title: One test in a set
senses.definition: one of several tests used together to compare choices
senses.definitionCN: 几项测试之一，共同用来比较各种选择
senses.example: The committee listed five criteria for the award.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为这个奖项列了五项评判指标。
senses.why: A single test can be fooled; several together rarely are.
senses.whyCN: 单独一项测试容易被骗，几项一起就很难。

senses.title: A rule for sorting
senses.definition: a rule used to put things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 用来把事物分进各组的规则
senses.example: Size is a useful criterion for sorting the samples.
senses.exampleCN: 大小是给样本分类的一个有用依据。
senses.why: To sort is to decide, and every decision needs a rule.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是做决定，而每个决定都需要一条规则。

intro.en: Criterion comes from Greek kriterion, a means of judging, from krites, a judge.
intro.cn: criterion 源自希腊语 kriterion（判断的手段），再往上是 krites（法官）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate, to decide or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开、决定或判断。

items.en: Krites named a judge or an interpreter.
items.cn: krites 指法官或解释者。

items.en: Kriterion named the tool or test used to judge.
items.cn: kriterion 指用来判断的工具或检验。

items.en: Criterion entered English as a word for a test of truth.
items.cn: criterion 作为检验真伪的词进入英语。

items.en: It spread to science, business and daily choices.

scene: 编辑把稿子退回来，页边全是红笔字。Her criticism was sharp but useful.
sceneCN: 这里 criticism 指「批评」（第 1 个义项：指出缺点与问题的评判）；句意是她的批评尖锐但有用。

senses.title: The act of finding faults
senses.definition: the act of saying what is wrong with someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人或某事哪里不对的行为
senses.example: He took the criticism calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静地接受了批评。
senses.why: A fault named clearly can be repaired.
senses.whyCN: 被清楚指出的毛病，才有机会修好。

senses.title: A judgement of a work
senses.definition: a careful written or spoken judgement of a book, play or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对书籍、戏剧或观点作出的细致评判
senses.example: She wrote a criticism of the new novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这部新小说写了一篇评论。
senses.why: Judgement can praise as well as blame.
senses.whyCN: 评判既能责备，也能称赞。

senses.title: The study of literature
senses.definition: the academic study and judgement of literary works
senses.definitionCN: 对文学作品进行的学术研究与评判
senses.example: He teaches literary criticism at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大学教文学批评。
senses.why: A whole discipline grew from the habit of judging texts.
senses.whyCN: 一整门学科，就是从评判文本的习惯里长出来的。

intro.en: Criticism joins critic, from Greek kritikos, with the suffix -ism.
intro.cn: criticism 由 critic（源自希腊语 kritikos）加后缀 -ism 构成。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate and to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开与判断。

items.en: Kritikos described a person able to judge.
items.cn: kritikos 形容有能力判断的人。

items.en: Criticus named the judge of a text.
items.cn: criticus 指评判文本的人。

items.en: Criticism named the work of a critic.
items.cn: criticism 指评论家所做的工作。

items.en: It also meant the pointing out of faults.
items.cn: 它也开始指指出缺点。

items.en: It now covers both blame and scholarly judgement.
items.cn: 今天它兼指责备与学术评判。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the critic- stem, and the meaning group names other acts of judging aloud.
note.cn: 形近组共享 critic- 词干，近义组列出其他公开评判的说法。

entries.definition: a published judgement of a new work
entries.definitionCN: 对新作品公开发表的评判

entries.definition: the feeling that something is wrong

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with red ink and end with a whole shelf of theory.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从红墨水开始，最后落到整整一架理论书。

normal.en: Critic plus -ism: the habit that a critic lives by.
normal.cn: critic 加 -ism：评论家赖以为生的那个习惯。

normal.en: Red ink on a margin is a map of what to fix.
normal.cn: 页边的红字，是一张该修哪里的地图。

normal.en: Good criticism leaves the work standing, only straighter.
normal.cn: 好的批评让作品仍站着，只是更直。

normal.en: The word can praise; blame only got there first.
normal.cn: 这个词也能称赞，只是责备先占了位置。

normal.en: A shelf of theory began with one sharp remark.
normal.cn: 一架理论书，始于一句尖锐的话。

abstract.en: Picture a page with more red than black.
abstract.cn: 想象一页红字比黑字还多的稿子。

abstract.en: Picture a polite letter that still stings.
abstract.cn: 想象一封客气却仍然刺人的信。

abstract.en: Picture a lecture hall arguing over one line.
abstract.cn: 想象阶梯教室里为一句话争论。

examples.en: She accepted the criticism without anger.
examples.cn: 她毫无怒气地接受了批评。

examples.en: The report offers useful criticism of the design.
examples.cn: 这份报告对设计提出了有用的批评。

examples.en: He is reading modern literary criticism.
examples.cn: 他正在读现代文学批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 criticism 记成 critic（评论家）加 -ism：评论家干的那件事，就是评判，也包括挑毛病。

root: 由 critic（源自希腊语 kritikos，善于判断的）加 -ism 构成；本义是「评论家所做之事」，后兼指指出缺点与对作品的学术评判。

sensesIntro.en: From naming a fault, to judging a work, to a discipline built on judging.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指出一处毛病，到评判一部作品，再到建立在评判之上的学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red ink filling the margin of a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：页边被红墨水写满的稿子。

branches.en: Naming a fault is the first use of the word.
branches.cn: 指出毛病，是这个词最早的用法。

branches.en: A full judgement weighs merits as well as faults.
branches.cn: 完整的评判既称缺点，也称优点。

branches.en: The habit of judging became a field of study.
branches.cn: 评判的习惯，长成了一门学问。

branches.en: Both blame and praise are forms of judgement.
branches.cn: 责备与称赞，都是评判的形式。

branches.en: A review and a thesis can share the same method.
branches.cn: 一篇书评和一篇论文，可以用同一套方法。

intro.en: Criticism is critic plus -ism, the suffix that names a practice or a doctrine.
intro.cn: criticism 是 critic 加 -ism，这个后缀表示一种做法或主张。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back through Latin criticus to Greek krinein, to judge.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干经拉丁语 criticus 上溯到希腊语 krinein（判断）。

items.example: The critic read the draft twice.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把稿子读了两遍。

items.example: Her notes were critical but kind.

items.exampleCN: 带着判断去读这份稿子。

definition_en: plates, bowls and cups used for eating
core_image: 一摞洗好的盘子立在沥水架上
scene: 她把餐具一件件亲手洗净。She washed every piece of crockery by hand.

senses.title: Plates and dishes
senses.definition: plates, bowls and cups used at table

senses.example: The crockery was stacked by the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 餐具堆在水槽边。
senses.why: A tower of clean plates.
senses.whyCN: 一摞干净的盘子。

senses.title: Earthenware
senses.definition: dishes made of baked clay
senses.definitionCN: 黏土烧制的器皿
senses.example: The kitchen sells local crockery.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖本地陶器。
senses.why: Clay warmed into a bowl.
senses.whyCN: 烧成碗的黏土。

senses.title: A full set
senses.definition: a matching set for the table
senses.definitionCN: 配套的一套餐具
senses.example: They bought new crockery for the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为公寓买了新餐具。
senses.why: Cups and plates that match.
senses.whyCN: 花色相配的杯盘。

intro.en: Crockery joins crock, an old word for a clay pot, with the suffix -ery, meaning a group of things.
intro.cn: crockery 由 crock（旧指陶罐）加后缀 -ery（一类事物）构成。

items.en: Croc meant a clay pot.
items.cn: croc 意为陶罐。

items.en: Crokke kept the pot sense.
items.cn: crokke 保留陶罐义。

items.en: Crock named an earthen pot.
items.cn: 十五世纪 crock 指陶制器皿。

items.en: Crockery named table dishes as a group.
items.cn: 十八世纪 crockery 统称餐具。

items.en: Crockery named a household set.
items.cn: 十九世纪 crockery 指家用成套餐具。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crock stem; the near-meaning group names table dishes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crock 词干；近义组都是餐具。

normalIntro.en: Crockery is a whole family of crocks, the clay pots that became plates and cups.
normalIntro.cn: crockery 就是一大家子 crock——由陶罐变成的盘碗杯。

normal.en: A crock is an old clay pot.
normal.cn: crock 是旧时的陶罐。

normal.en: The suffix -ery means a group of things.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ery 表示一类事物。

normal.en: So crockery is a group of clay dishes.
normal.cn: 因此 crockery 就是一组陶制餐具。

normal.en: Plates and cups count as crockery.
normal.cn: 盘子和杯子都算餐具。

normal.en: Crockery must be washed by hand.
normal.cn: 餐具要手洗。

abstract.en: A tower of clean plates.

examples.en: The crockery rattled on the tray.
examples.cn: 餐具在托盘上叮当作响。

examples.en: Please put the crockery away.
examples.cn: 请把餐具收起来。

examples.en: All the crockery was made by hand.
examples.cn: 所有餐具都是手工做的。

root: 古英语 croc（陶罐）+ -ery（一类事物）→ crockery

sensesIntro.cn: 所有上桌的陶制器皿。

definition_zh: n. 鳄鱼；成队行走的人
definition_en: a large river reptile with a long body and strong jaws
core_image: 只露出眼睛和鼻孔的鳞背浮在水面
scene: 鳄鱼只把眼睛露出水面。The crocodile showed only its eyes above the water.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：crocodile 指鳄鱼；句意是鳄鱼只把眼睛露在水面上。

senses.title: The reptile
senses.definition: a large reptile that lives in rivers
senses.definitionCN: 生活在河里的大型爬行动物
senses.example: The crocodile waited by the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 鳄鱼在岸边等候。
senses.why: Two eyes above still water.
senses.whyCN: 静水上的一双眼睛。

senses.title: Its skin
senses.definition: the skin or leather of this animal
senses.definitionCN: 这种动物的皮或皮革
senses.example: Her bag is made of crocodile.
senses.exampleCN: 她的包是鳄鱼皮做的。
senses.why: A row of raised scales.
senses.whyCN: 一排凸起的鳞片。

senses.title: A walking line
senses.definition: a long line of people walking together, in British use
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法指成队行走的人群
senses.example: The children walked in a crocodile.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排成一队走。
senses.why: Small hands on small shoulders.
senses.whyCN: 搭在小肩膀上的小手。

intro.en: Crocodile comes from Greek krokodilos, through Latin crocodilus.
intro.cn: crocodile 来自希腊语 krokodilos，经拉丁语 crocodilus 传入英语。

items.en: Krokodilos named the river reptile.
items.cn: krokodilos 指河中的鳄鱼。

items.en: Crocodilus kept the reptile sense.
items.cn: crocodilus 保留鳄鱼义。

items.en: Cocodril named the animal.
items.cn: 十三世纪 cocodril 指鳄鱼。

items.en: Crocodile fixed the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪 crocodile 定型为今拼写。

items.en: A crocodile named a line of walkers.
items.cn: 十九世纪英式用法指排队行走的人。

note.cn: 形近组都以 croc- 开头；近义组都是爬行动物与捕食者。

normal.en: Only its eyes and nostrils show.

normal.en: Its jaws are full of sharp teeth.

normal.en: Crocodile tears are pretend tears.

scene: 警察在边境抓住了那个骗子。The police caught the crook at the border.

senses.why: A card hidden up a sleeve.

senses.title: A bend

senses.why: A branch curving back.

senses.definitionCN: 把某物弯成弧形

core_image: 一整片麦田在风里翻成金色的浪

senses.title: Plants grown for food

senses.definitionCN: 大量种植以供食用或出售的植物

senses.whyCN: 人决定种什么，而这个决定塑造了整片田。

senses.why: New students come up together, like grain in one field.
senses.whyCN: 新生一起冒出来，就像同一片田里的庄稼。

intro.en: Crop comes from Old English cropp, the top or head of a plant.
intro.cn: crop 源自古英语 cropp，指植物的顶端或穗。

items.en: Cropp meant the top or head of a plant.
items.cn: cropp 指植物的顶端或穗头。

items.en: It also named a bird's craw.
items.cn: 它也指鸟的嗉囊。

items.en: Crop named the grain gathered from a field.
items.cn: crop 指从田里收上来的谷物。

items.en: It came to mean a whole season of harvest.
items.cn: 它开始指一整季的收成。

items.en: It was used for hair cut close to the head.
items.cn: 它被用来指剪得很短的头发。

items.en: It also means a group appearing at one time.
items.cn: 它也指同时出现的一批。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cropp- spelling, and the meaning group names other farm products.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cropp- 这串拼写，近义组列出其他农产说法。

entries.definition: cut short, or cut off at the edges
entries.definitionCN: 剪短的，或被裁去边缘的

entries.definition: the gathering in of a season's crops
entries.definitionCN: 把一季作物收上来的过程

entries.definition: the amount a field or farm gives
entries.definitionCN: 一块田或农场产出的数量

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a golden field and end with a new class in September.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一片金色的田开始，最后落到九月新来的一班学生。

normal.en: Crop is what the top of a plant becomes in our hands.
normal.cn: crop 就是植物顶端最终落到我们手里的东西。

normal.en: One summer becomes one number.
normal.cn: 一个夏天，最后变成一个数字。

normal.en: A cut of hair and a cut of grain share the word.
normal.cn: 剪头发和割庄稼，用的是同一个词。

normal.en: Problems crop up like weeds: suddenly, and in groups.
normal.cn: 麻烦像杂草一样冒出来：突然，而且成群。

normal.en: New students are a crop: they come up together.
normal.cn: 新生就是一批庄稼：一起冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture wheat bending in one long wave.
abstract.cn: 想象麦子弯成一道长长的浪。

abstract.en: Picture a hand full of fresh grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手捧着新收的谷粒。

abstract.en: Picture a gate full of new faces.
abstract.cn: 想象门口挤满新面孔。

examples.en: Farmers here grow three crops a year.
examples.cn: 这里的农民一年种三季作物。

examples.en: The corn crop survived the dry summer.
examples.cn: 玉米收成熬过了干旱的夏天。

examples.en: A new crop of problems cropped up at once.
examples.cn: 一批新问题一下子冒了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crop 记成从植物顶端割下来的那一把：一季的庄稼，就是收成。

root: 源自古英语 cropp（植物顶端、穗），后指从田里收上来的谷物，再引申为一季的收成、同时出现的一批，以及剪短的动作。

sensesIntro.en: From what grows in the field, to what the field gives, to a group that arrives together.
sensesIntro.cn: 从田里种的东西，到田里给出的收成，再到一起到来的一批。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field of wheat turning gold in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：风里翻成金色的麦田。

branches.en: The planted plants are the crop itself.
branches.cn: 种下去的植物本身就是作物。

branches.en: The gathered amount is the season's crop.
branches.cn: 收回来的数量，就是这一季的收成。

branches.en: A group arriving together borrows the field image.
branches.cn: 同时到来的一批，借用了田里的意象。

branches.en: What is planted and what is gathered share one word.
branches.cn: 种下的和收回的，共用一个词。

branches.en: Both a harvest and a class are counted as one lot.
branches.cn: 收成和一个班，都被算作一整批。

intro.en: Crop is a short Old English word that builds compounds like cropland and sharecropper.
intro.cn: crop 是古英语的短词，能组成 cropland、sharecropper 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin base is involved; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基，它是英语本族词。

items.example: The crop stood tall in June.

items.exampleCN: 这些田里种着两季作物。

items.meaning: the act of growing or cutting
a farmer who pays rent in crops
items.exampleCN: 这位分成制农民留下三分之一。

items.meaning: a season with almost no harvest

definition_en: a word puzzle played on a grid of squares
core_image: 黑白方格交错，词与词在格子里咬合
scene: 爷爷每天早上都做填字游戏。Grandpa does the crossword every morning.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：crossword 指填字游戏；句意是爷爷每天早上都做填字游戏。

senses.title: The puzzle
senses.definition: a puzzle in which words cross on a grid
senses.definitionCN: 词语在方格上交错的谜题
senses.example: She finished the crossword in ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她十分钟就做完了填字游戏。
senses.why: Words locking into a grid.
senses.whyCN: 咬进方格的词。

senses.title: The grid
senses.definition: the pattern of white and black squares
senses.definitionCN: 黑白方格组成的版式
senses.example: The crossword had one black square.
senses.exampleCN: 这个填字游戏只有一个黑格。
senses.why: Black squares like gaps in a wall.
senses.whyCN: 像墙缝一样的黑格。

senses.title: A cryptic form
senses.definition: a harder version with tricky clues
senses.definitionCN: 提示曲折的难版
senses.example: He loves the cryptic crossword.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢隐晦填字游戏。
senses.why: A clue hiding its answer.
senses.whyCN: 藏着答案的提示。

intro.en: Crossword joins cross and word, and named a puzzle printed in a New York newspaper in 1913.
intro.cn: crossword 由 cross（交叉）与 word（词）合成，1913 年首次出现在纽约报纸的谜题中。

items.en: Cros meant a crossing shape.
items.cn: cros 意为交叉形。

items.en: Word meant a spoken unit.
items.cn: word 意为词语。

items.en: A newspaper printed the first crossword.
items.cn: 1913 年《纽约世界报》刊出首个填字谜。

items.en: British papers adopted the crossword.
items.cn: 二十世纪二十年代英国报纸引入填字游戏。

items.en: Cryptic crosswords added tricky clues.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代出现隐晦提示版。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cross or word element; the near-meaning group names puzzles.
note.cn: 形近组含 cross 或 word；近义组都是谜题。

entries.definition: A mark or shape of two lines.
A question with a clever answer.
A problem that makes you think.

normalIntro.en: A crossword is words that cross, locking into a grid.
normalIntro.cn: crossword 就是互相交叉、咬进方格的词。

normal.en: Cross means to go across.
normal.cn: cross 意为交叉、横过。

normal.en: A word is a unit of language.
normal.cn: word 意为词。

normal.en: Crosswords lock words across and down.
normal.cn: 填字游戏的词横竖交错。

normal.en: Clues point to each answer.
normal.cn: 提示语指向每个答案。

normal.en: Quick crosswords are easy; cryptic ones are hard.
normal.cn: 简易版容易，隐晦版很难。

abstract.en: Words locking into a grid.
abstract.cn: 咬进方格的词。

abstract.en: Black squares like gaps in a wall.
abstract.cn: 像墙缝一样的黑格。

abstract.en: A clue hiding its answer.
abstract.cn: 藏着答案的提示。

examples.en: He solved the crossword before breakfast.
examples.cn: 他早饭前就做完了填字游戏。

examples.en: The crossword clue was very hard.
examples.cn: 这道填字提示非常难。

examples.en: Crosswords keep the mind active.
examples.cn: 填字游戏让头脑保持活跃。

dict_mnemonic.text: cross（交叉）+ word（词）→ 词与词交叉的谜题，即填字游戏。

root: cross（交叉）+ word（词）→ crossword（1913 年出现的谜题名）

sensesIntro.en: Words crossing in a grid of squares.
sensesIntro.cn: 在方格中彼此交叉的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words crossing and locking inside a grid
core.cn: 核心意象：词在方格中交叉咬合

branches.en: Words locking into a grid.
branches.cn: 咬进方格的词。

branches.en: Black squares like gaps in a wall.
branches.cn: 像墙缝一样的黑格。

branches.en: A clue hiding its answer.
branches.cn: 藏着答案的提示。

branches.en: A page full of small doors.
branches.cn: 满是小小门洞的一页。

branches.en: A grid that guards its answers.
branches.cn: 守着答案的方格。

intro.en: Crossword is a modern English compound of cross and word.
intro.cn: crossword 是 cross 与 word 组成的现代英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin crux means cross, and verbum means word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux 意为十字，verbum 意为词。

definition_en: a large number of people gathered close together, or to fill a place
core_image: 广场上人挤人，连转身的地方都没有
scene: 广场上人挤人，连转身都困难。A crowd had gathered outside the station.
sceneCN: 这里 crowd 指「人群」（第 1 个义项：密集聚在一起的一大群人）；句意是车站外已经聚起了一群人。

senses.title: Many people in one place
senses.definition: a large number of people gathered close together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 密集聚集在同一地点的一大群人
senses.example: The crowd cheered as the team scored.
senses.exampleCN: 球队得分时人群欢呼起来。
senses.why: Many bodies in a small space become one moving thing.
senses.whyCN: 许多身体挤在狭小空间里，就变成一具会移动的东西。

senses.title: Ordinary people as a whole
senses.definition: the mass of ordinary people, not leaders or experts
senses.definitionCN: 普通人的整体，而非领袖或专家
senses.example: The song was first sung by the crowd, not the choir.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌先由群众唱起来，而不是唱诗班。
senses.why: A mass of people can be spoken of as a single force.
senses.whyCN: 一大群人，可以被当成一股力量来说。

senses.title: Fill a place tightly
senses.definition: to fill a space so that there is little room left
senses.definitionCN: 把空间填满，几乎不留余地
senses.example: Fans crowded the entrance before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天没亮粉丝就挤满了入口。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb when the mass starts to press in.
senses.whyCN: 当人群开始往里压，名词就变成了动词。

intro.en: Crowd comes from Old English crudan, to press or push.
intro.cn: crowd 源自古英语 crudan，意为挤压、推。

items.en: Crudan meant to press or push.
items.cn: crudan 意为挤压或推。

items.en: Croude named a pushing throng of people.
items.cn: croude 指互相推挤的一群人。

items.en: Crowd named a large company of people.
items.cn: crowd 指一大群人。

items.en: The verb meant to press into a place.
items.cn: 动词形式意为挤进一个地方。

items.en: It spread to any tightly packed group.
items.cn: 它扩展到任何紧密挤在一起的一群。

items.en: It also means ordinary people as a whole.
items.cn: 它也指整体意义上的普通群众。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crowd spelling, and the meaning group names other large groups of people.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crowd 这串拼写，近义组列出其他大群人的说法。

entries.definition: the act of pressing into a space
a crowd that may become violent
people gathered to watch or listen
entries.definitionCN: 聚起来观看或倾听的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with bodies pressed together and end with a voice called the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从挤在一起的身体开始，最后落到被称为人民的那个声音。

normal.en: Crowd comes from pushing: many shoulders in one doorway.
normal.cn: crowd 来自推挤：一道门口挤着许多肩膀。

normal.en: One face is a person; a thousand faces are a crowd.
normal.cn: 一张脸是一个人，一千张脸就是人群。

normal.en: A crowd has no single mind, yet it moves as one.
normal.cn: 人群没有统一的头脑，却能像一个整体那样移动。

normal.en: When people press in, the noun becomes a verb.
normal.cn: 人往里一挤，名词就变成了动词。

normal.en: Stand out from the crowd by standing still.
normal.cn: 想从人群里显出来，就站住不动。

abstract.en: Picture a square filled shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象广场上肩挨着肩。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred hands raised at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一百只手同时举起。

abstract.en: Picture one voice coming out of many mouths.
abstract.cn: 想象许多张嘴里传出同一个声音。

examples.en: A crowd gathered to watch the street singer.
examples.cn: 一群人聚起来看街头歌手。

examples.en: The crowd pushed toward the open gate.
examples.cn: 人群朝敞开的大门挤去。

examples.en: Tourists crowd the old town every summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天游客挤满这座老城。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crowd 记成一道门口挤满的肩膀：人一多、一挤，就成了人群。

root: 源自古英语 crudan（挤压、推）；本义是「互相推挤的一群人」，由挤压的动作生出人群之义，再作动词表示挤满、聚集。

sensesIntro.en: From bodies packed in one place, to the people as a whole, to the act of pressing in.
sensesIntro.cn: 从挤在一处的身体，到作为整体的群众，再到往里挤的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoulders packed tight in a square.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上紧紧相挨的肩膀。

branches.en: A tight mass of people becomes a single presence.
branches.cn: 密集的一群人，变成一个有存在感的东西。

branches.en: The same mass can stand for ordinary people.
branches.cn: 同一群人，也能代表普通民众。

branches.en: When the mass presses in, the word turns into a verb.
branches.cn: 当这群人往里压，这个词就变成动词。

branches.en: A crowd can be counted and also spoken of as one force.
branches.cn: 人群既能被计数，也能被当成一股力量。

branches.en: People in the street both are the crowd and crowd the street.
branches.cn: 街上的人既是人群，也在挤满街道。

intro.en: Crowd is a native English word that builds crowded, crowding and overcrowded.
intro.cn: crowd 是英语本族词，能组成 crowded、crowding 与 overcrowded。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word grew from the old verb for pressing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基，它从表示挤压的古动词长出来。

items.example: The crowding at the gate was dangerous.
The square stood crowdless at dawn.

items.meaning: keeping a large group safe and orderly

definition_en: a circle worn on the head by a ruler, or the top part of something
core_image: 一顶镶着宝石的金冠稳稳压在王座上方那颗头上
scene: 加冕那天，金冠被缓缓放到新王头上。The crown passed to his daughter.
sceneCN: 这里 crown 指「王冠」（第 1 个义项：君主戴在头上的环形饰物）；句意是王冠传给了他的女儿。

senses.title: A ruler's circle of gold
senses.definition: a circle of gold and jewels worn on the head by a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 君主戴在头上的金玉环形饰物
senses.example: The crown sat on a velvet cushion.
senses.exampleCN: 王冠放在一只天鹅绒垫子上。
senses.why: A circle on the head marks the one who stands above all.
senses.whyCN: 头顶一个圆环，标出那个高过所有人的人。

senses.title: Royal power itself
senses.definition: the power or position of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王所拥有的权力或地位
senses.example: He gave up the crown for love.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了爱放弃了王位。
senses.why: The object stands for the office it marks.
senses.whyCN: 那件实物，代表了它所标记的那个位置。

senses.title: The highest part
senses.definition: the top or highest part of a head, a tree or a hill
senses.definitionCN: 头、树或山最高的那部分
senses.example: A bird sat on the crown of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸟停在树顶。
senses.why: The top of anything wears a small crown of its own.
senses.whyCN: 任何东西的顶部，都自带一顶小冠。

intro.en: Crown comes from Latin corona, a wreath, through Old French corone.
intro.cn: crown 源自拉丁语 corona（花环），经古法语 corone 进入英语。

items.en: Corona meant a wreath or a circle.
items.cn: corona 指花环或圆环。

items.en: It was given to victors and to brides.
items.cn: 它被戴在胜利者与新娘头上。

items.en: Corone named a royal circlet.
items.cn: corone 指君王所戴的环形冠。

items.en: Crown named the king's circlet.
items.cn: crown 指国王的环形冠冕。

items.en: It came to mean royal power itself.
items.cn: 它开始指王权本身。

items.en: It also names the top of a head, a hill or a tooth.
items.cn: 它也指头、山或牙齿的顶部。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crown spelling, and the meaning group names other seats or signs of royal power.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crown 这串拼写，近义组列出其他王权的象征与位置。

entries.definition: having a crown, or made king
entries.definitionCN: 戴着王冠的，或被立为王的

entries.definition: without a crown or a ruler
the seat and office of a ruler
a small crown worn by a noble
a ring of leaves or flowers

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a ring of gold and end with the top of an old tree.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个金环开始，最后落到一棵老树的顶梢。

normal.en: Crown began as a wreath, and a wreath is a circle.
normal.cn: crown 本是花环，而花环就是一个圆。

normal.en: A circle has no beginning, which suits a king.
normal.cn: 圆没有起点，这正合一位君王。

normal.en: The crown is heavy because the office is.
normal.cn: 冠很重，因为那个位置很重。

normal.en: Every hill wears its own crown of trees.
normal.cn: 每一座山都戴着属于自己的树冠。

normal.en: To crown a day is to give it a perfect end.
normal.cn: 为一天加冕，就是给它一个完美的结尾。

abstract.en: Picture gold resting on red velvet.
abstract.cn: 想象金子搁在红色天鹅绒上。

abstract.en: Picture a head bowed to receive a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗低下去接住圆环的头。

abstract.en: Picture a single tree above the whole forest.
abstract.cn: 想象整片林子之上的一棵树。

examples.en: The crown was kept in a locked room.
examples.cn: 王冠被锁在一间屋子里。

examples.en: She succeeded to the crown at twenty.
examples.cn: 她二十岁继承王位。

examples.en: Snow crowned the top of the mountain.
examples.cn: 雪覆盖了山顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crown 记成头顶上那个金环：戴上它是王冠，戴在山上就是山顶。

root: 源自拉丁语 corona（花环、圆环），经古法语 corone 进入英语；本义是戴在头上的环，后指王冠与王权，再引申为任何事物的顶部。

sensesIntro.en: From a circle on a head, to the power it stands for, to the top of anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头上的一只圆环，到它所代表的权力，再到任何事物的顶端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold ring resting on a bowed head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只金环落在低下的头顶。

branches.en: The ring itself is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 那只圆环本身，是最早的意思。

branches.en: The object then stands for the power behind it.
branches.cn: 这件实物随后代表了它背后的权力。

branches.en: Any highest point is crowned by its own top.
branches.cn: 任何最高处，都被自己的顶端加冕。

branches.en: Gold and authority are worn together.
branches.cn: 金子和权威，被一起戴在头上。

branches.en: A king and a hill both carry a crown.
branches.cn: 国王和山丘，都顶着一顶冠。

intro.en: Crown is a short word that builds crowned, crowning and uncrowned.
intro.cn: crown 是个短词，能组成 crowned、crowning 与 uncrowned。

latinIntro.en: The Latin corona, a wreath, is the source of crown and of coronation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 corona（花环）是 crown 与 coronation 的源头。

items.meaning: a ring worn by a ruler
items.example: The crown shone under the lamp.
Two crowns were kept in the vault.
The king was crowned at dawn.

items.exampleCN: 最辉煌的一刻出现在最后。

items.example: The crownless prince left the hall.
items.exampleCN: 未戴冠的王子离开了大厅。

items.example: The coronation drew a huge crowd.

items.meaning: a small crown of a noble
items.example: A thin coronet held her hair.
items.exampleCN: 一顶细小的冠束住她的头发。

definition_en: extremely important because everything else depends on it
core_image: 一座窄桥只容一人通过，桥下是深谷
scene: 队伍走到一座窄桥前，桥下是深谷。One wrong step would be crucial for the whole climb.
sceneCN: 这里 crucial 指「至关重要的」（第 1 个义项：整个结果都取决于它的）；句意是走错一步，对整次攀登都至关重要。

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.definition: so important that the whole outcome depends on it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到整个结果都取决于它
senses.example: Sleep is crucial for memory.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠对记忆至关重要。
senses.why: One thing can hold up everything that comes after it.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西，就能撑住它之后的全部。

senses.title: Decisive at a turning point
senses.definition: settling the result at one particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某个特定时刻把结果定下来
senses.example: That vote was crucial to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那次投票对这项计划是决定性的。
senses.why: Where two roads part, one step decides the rest.
senses.whyCN: 两条路分岔的地方，一步就定下余下的路。

intro.en: Crucial comes from Latin crux, a cross, through Medieval Latin crucialis.
intro.cn: crucial 源自拉丁语 crux（十字），经中世纪拉丁语 crucialis 而来。

items.en: Crux meant a cross, where two lines met.
items.cn: crux 指十字，是两条线相交之处。

items.en: Crucialis meant belonging to a cross.
items.cn: crucialis 意为与十字有关的。

items.en: A crossroad forced a traveller to choose.
items.cn: 十字路口迫使行人做出选择。

items.en: Crucial first meant shaped like a cross.
items.cn: crucial 最初意为十字形的。

items.en: It took the sense of decisive, like a crossroad.
items.cn: 它取得如十字路口般「决定性」的意思。

items.en: It now simply means extremely important.
items.cn: 今天它只表示极其重要。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cruc- stem, and the meaning group names other words for what decides an outcome.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cruc- 词干，近义组列出其他表示决定成败的说法。

entries.definition: a mark or shape of two lines
entries.definitionCN: 两条线构成的记号或形状

entries.definition: the central point of a problem
in a way that decides everything
so important that the result depends on it

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at a narrow bridge and end at a crossroad with no sign.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一座窄桥开始，最后落到一个没有路牌的十字路口。

normal.en: Crucial hides a cross: a place where you must choose.
normal.cn: crucial 里藏着一个十字：那是你必须选的地方。

normal.en: One step on a narrow bridge decides the climb.
normal.cn: 窄桥上的第一步，定下整次攀登。

normal.en: Not everything matters; one thing matters most.
normal.cn: 不是一切都重要，只有一样最重要。

normal.en: At a crossroad, both roads look the same in the dark.
normal.cn: 在十字路口，黑暗里两条路看起来一模一样。

normal.en: Say crucial when the whole plan hangs on it.
normal.cn: 整个计划都挂在上面时，就说至关重要。

abstract.en: Picture a plank over a deep gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板横在深沟上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a rail, holding steady.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶住栏杆，稳住不动。

abstract.en: Picture two roads splitting with no sign.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路分开，却没有路牌。

examples.en: Clean water is crucial to public health.
examples.cn: 清洁的水对公共健康至关重要。

examples.en: The next ten minutes were crucial.
examples.cn: 接下来的十分钟是决定性的。

examples.en: Trust plays a crucial role in any team.
examples.cn: 信任在任何团队里都起关键作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crucial 记成一个十字路口：往左往右全看这一步，所以它至关重要。

root: 源自拉丁语 crux（十字）与中世纪拉丁语 crucialis；本义是「十字形的」，因十字路口必须做出抉择，19 世纪起引申为决定性的、至关重要的。

sensesIntro.en: From the weight of one thing, to the moment that settles the rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一样东西的分量，到把余下一切定下来的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow bridge over a deep gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：横在深沟上的一座窄桥。

branches.en: One factor carries the weight of all the others.
branches.cn: 一个因素，扛着其余全部因素的分量。

branches.en: At a crossroad, a single step settles the direction.
branches.cn: 在十字路口，一步就定下方向。

branches.en: What is decisive is decisive because it is needed.
branches.cn: 决定性的东西之所以决定性，是因为它被需要。

branches.en: Remove it, and the whole plan falls.
branches.cn: 把它抽走，整个计划就塌了。

branches.en: The moment is small, but everything hangs on it.
branches.cn: 那一刻很小，可一切都挂在它上面。

intro.en: Crucial is built on the Latin crux, a cross, with the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: crucial 建在拉丁语 crux（十字）之上，加了形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crux also gives cross, crux and crusade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux 还生出 cross、crux 与 crusade。

items.meaning: in a way that decides the result
items.example: Crucially, the door was left open.
The report stressed the cruciality of water.
items.exampleCN: 报告强调了水的重要性。
一个十字标出了那个地点。

items.meaning: the central point of a problem
items.example: That is the crux of the matter.
She led a crusade for clean air.
items.exampleCN: 她发起了一场争取清洁空气的运动。

items.example: The church has a cruciform plan.
items.exampleCN: 这座教堂是十字形平面。

items.meaning: to put to death on a cross
items.example: The story says he was crucified.
items.exampleCN: 故事说他被钉上了十字架。

definition_zh: 天然的；粗糙的；粗鲁的；粗略的
definition_en: in a raw natural state, made without skill, or said without tact
core_image: 从井口直接舀起的一勺原油，还混着泥沙
scene: 工地上有人从桶里舀出一勺还混着泥沙的原油。They loaded the crude oil straight onto the truck.
sceneCN: 这里 crude 指「天然的、未加工的」（第 1 个义项：从地下取出后还没提炼的）；句意是他们把原油直接装上卡车。

pos.zh: 天然的；粗糙的；粗鲁的；粗略的

senses.title: Raw, unrefined
senses.definition: in a natural state and not yet processed
senses.definitionCN: 处于自然状态、尚未加工的
senses.example: The refinery turns crude oil into fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 炼油厂把原油变成燃料。
senses.why: What comes out of the ground must be cleaned before use.
senses.whyCN: 从地下出来的东西，用前总要先洗净。

senses.title: Roughly made
senses.definition: made quickly and without skill or care
senses.definitionCN: 做得快而缺乏技艺或用心
senses.example: He built a crude shelter from branches.
senses.exampleCN: 他用树枝搭了个粗糙的棚子。
senses.why: Untrained hands leave their marks on what they make.
senses.whyCN: 没练过的手，会在做的东西上留下痕迹。

senses.title: Rude, without tact
senses.definition: said or done in a way that shocks or offends people
senses.definitionCN: 以令人震惊或冒犯的方式说出或做出
senses.example: His crude remark silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句粗鲁的话让全场安静下来。
senses.why: A missing polish in words cuts like a rough edge.
senses.whyCN: 话里少了打磨，就像毛边一样割人。

intro.en: Crude comes from Latin crudus, raw or unripe, through Old French crud.
intro.cn: crude 源自拉丁语 crudus（生的、未熟的），经古法语 crud 进入英语。

items.en: Crudus described food that was raw or not cooked.
items.cn: crudus 形容生的、没煮过的食物。

items.en: It also meant unripe, or hard to digest.
items.cn: 它也表示未成熟、难以消化。

items.en: Crud kept both the raw and the unripe senses.
items.cn: crud 同时保留了生与未熟两层意思。

items.en: Crude first described raw food and unripe fruit.
items.cn: crude 最初形容生食与未熟的水果。

items.en: It spread to rough work and rude words.
items.cn: 它扩展到粗糙的手艺与粗鲁的言语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cru- opening, and the meaning group names things still in a raw state.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cru- 开头，近义组列出仍处于原始状态的说法。

entries.definition: the hard outer layer of bread
a very small piece of bread

entries.definitionCN: 不平滑或未精细完成的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with something pulled from the ground and end with words that cut.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一件刚出土的东西开始，落到几句会割人的话上。

normal.en: Crude is the state before the factory touches it.
normal.cn: crude 是工厂还没碰过它时的状态。

normal.en: A crude chair still holds you up, but it wobbles.
normal.cn: 粗糙的椅子仍能撑住你，只是会晃。

normal.en: Crude words are words with the polish sanded off.
normal.cn: 粗鲁的话，是被磨掉了光的那层话。

normal.en: Raw oil, raw wood, raw manners: one word for all.
normal.cn: 原油、原木、没教养的举止：一个词全包。

normal.en: If it came straight out and skipped the finishing, it is crude.
normal.cn: 直接从里面出来、跳过了修饰的，就是 crude。

abstract.en: Picture oil black and thick, still smoking from the well.
abstract.cn: 想象又黑又稠的油，从井口还冒着气。

abstract.en: Picture a table made of one unplaned board.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只用一块没刨过的板做成的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a laugh that lands on the wrong face.
abstract.cn: 想象一声笑落在不该落的那张脸上。

examples.en: The crude oil is refined before it is sold.
examples.cn: 原油在出售前要先提炼。

examples.en: He made a crude table from three old boards.
examples.cn: 他用三块旧木板做了一张粗糙的桌子。

examples.en: Her crude comment hurt everyone at the table.
examples.cn: 她那句粗鲁的评论伤了在座所有人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crude 记成「生的」：原油、生手、生硬的话，都还没经过打磨。

root: 源自拉丁语 crudus（生的、未熟的），经古法语 crud 进入英语；本义是未经烹煮与提炼，后来引申为做得粗糙、说话粗鲁。

sensesIntro.en: From raw material, to rough work, to words that wound.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没加工的原料，到粗糙的手艺，再到伤人的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket of oil lifted straight from the well.
core.cn: 核心意象：一桶刚从井里提上来的原油。

branches.en: What the earth gives is used before it is cleaned.
branches.cn: 大地给出的东西，还没洗净就被用上。

branches.en: A thing made in a hurry keeps its rough edges.
branches.cn: 匆忙做出来的东西，会留着粗糙的边。

branches.en: A remark without polish can cut the listener.
branches.cn: 没打磨过的话，会割到听的人。

branches.en: Raw material and rough work share one word.
branches.cn: 原料与粗活共用一个词。

branches.en: Rough edges appear in things and in manners.
branches.cn: 粗糙的边既出现在物件上，也出现在举止里。

intro.en: Crude belongs to the Latin crudus family, where raw matter and rough manners meet.
intro.cn: crude 属于拉丁语 crudus 这一族，原料与粗鲁在这里相遇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crudus, raw or unripe, is the root under all these words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crudus（生的、未熟的）是这些词共同的根。

items.example: Crude oil burns with dark smoke.
The crudity of the plan shocked us.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划的粗糙让我们吃惊。

items.example: The crudeness of the joke upset her.
items.exampleCN: 那玩笑的粗俗让她不快。

items.example: Wash that crud off your hands.

items.meaning: raw vegetables served as a dish
items.exampleCN: 晚饭前他们上了生蔬菜拼盘。

items.meaning: the return of a disease or problem
items.example: Doctors feared a recrudescence of the fever.

items.meaning: oil as it comes from the ground

definition_zh: 残忍的；残酷的；令人痛苦的
definition_en: willing to make others suffer, or hard and painful to bear
core_image: 一只脚悬在一只小虫上方，迟迟不落下
scene: 孩子把蚂蚁扣在玻璃杯下，笑着看它乱撞。It was cruel to trap the ant and watch it struggle.
sceneCN: 这里 cruel 指「残忍的」（第 1 个义项：以别人的痛苦为乐）；句意是把蚂蚁扣住、看它挣扎，是很残忍的。

pos.zh: 残忍的；残酷的；令人痛苦的

senses.title: Pleased by pain
senses.definition: willing to cause pain and taking pleasure in it
senses.definitionCN: 愿意让别人痛苦，并以此取乐
senses.example: It is cruel to laugh at a child who falls.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑摔倒的孩子是残忍的。
senses.why: Pain should end a joke, never be its point.
senses.whyCN: 痛苦该让玩笑停下，而不该成为玩笑的目的。

senses.title: Causing suffering
senses.definition: causing pain, whether on purpose or not
senses.definitionCN: 无论有意与否都造成痛苦
senses.example: The long drought was cruel to the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的旱情对农民很残酷。
senses.why: The world can wound without any hand behind it.
senses.whyCN: 世界本身就会伤人，不需要谁在背后动手。

senses.title: Hard to bear
senses.definition: so hard or severe that it is painful to accept
senses.definitionCN: 艰难或严酷到令人难以接受
senses.example: Losing in the last minute was a cruel blow.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一刻输掉是沉重的一击。
senses.why: A fact can strike as hard as a fist.
senses.whyCN: 一个事实能像拳头一样砸下来。

intro.en: Cruel comes from Latin crudelis, hard-hearted, from crudus, raw.
intro.cn: cruel 源自拉丁语 crudelis（心硬的），其根是 crudus（生的）。

items.en: Crudelis described a hard heart that felt no pity.
items.cn: crudelis 形容一颗不觉怜悯的硬心。

items.en: It grew from crudus, raw, meaning not softened.
items.cn: 它出自 crudus（生的），意即没有软化。

items.en: Cruel named a person who took joy in pain.
items.cn: cruel 指以他人痛苦为乐的人。

items.en: Cruel entered English for harsh masters and hard acts.
items.cn: cruel 进入英语，用于严厉的主人与冷酷的行为。

items.en: It also describes fate, weather, and blows.
items.cn: 它也能形容命运、天气与打击。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cru- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of hardness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cru- 词干，近义组列出其他表示狠硬的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot held in the air and end with words that land like stones.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只停在半空的脚开始，落到像石头一样砸下的话。

normal.en: Cruel hearts do not feel the weight they press.
normal.cn: 狠心的人感觉不到自己压下去的分量。

normal.en: A joke that needs a victim is not a joke.
normal.cn: 需要一个受害者的玩笑，就不是玩笑。

normal.en: Fate can be cruel without having any hands.
normal.cn: 命运没有手，也能很残忍。

normal.en: The last minute is often the cruellest minute.
normal.cn: 最后一分钟常常是最残酷的一分钟。

normal.en: Cruel is what pity forgot to soften.
normal.cn: cruel 就是怜悯忘了去软化的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that stops just above a small insect.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手停在一只小虫上方。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd laughing and one person walking away.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人笑着，一个人转身走开。

abstract.en: Picture frost killing flowers that had just opened.
abstract.cn: 想象霜打死刚开的花。

examples.en: It is cruel to keep a large dog in a small cage.
examples.cn: 把大狗关在小笼子里是残忍的。

examples.en: The old king was cruel to those who disobeyed.
examples.cn: 老国王对不服从他的人很残酷。

examples.en: Losing the farm was a cruel lesson for the family.
examples.cn: 失去农场对这家人是残酷的一课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cruel 记成「心硬」：cru 是生的，el 像一道划痕，心没被软化，就会划伤别人。

root: 源自拉丁语 crudelis（心硬的、无情的），与 crudus（生的）同源，经古法语 cruel 进入英语；本义是心未软化，对他人的痛痒无感。

sensesIntro.en: From taking pleasure in pain, to causing it, to bearing what cannot be softened.
sensesIntro.cn: 从以别人的痛为乐，到造成痛苦，再到承受无法软化的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot held above a small insect.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚悬在一只小虫上方。

branches.en: A hard heart can watch pain and smile.
branches.cn: 硬起来的心能看着痛苦还笑。

branches.en: Harm may come from a will or from the world.
branches.cn: 伤害可能来自意志，也可能来自世界。

branches.en: Some blows are too heavy to soften.
branches.cn: 有些打击重得无法软化。

branches.en: The one who enjoys pain and the drought share a name.
branches.cn: 以痛苦为乐的人与旱情共用一个词。

branches.en: What hurts us is called cruel, whatever its source.
branches.cn: 凡是伤到我们的，不管来自哪里，都叫残忍。

intro.en: Cruel and crude share the Latin crudus, raw, which grew into two kinds of hardness.
intro.cn: cruel 与 crude 共享拉丁语 crudus（生的），后来长成两种不同的硬。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crudelis, hard-hearted, is the root behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crudelis（心硬的）是这一族词背后的根。

items.example: A cruel word can last for years.
items.exampleCN: 一句残忍的话能留很多年。

items.meaning: the act or habit of being cruel
items.example: The cruelty of the guard was well known.
items.exampleCN: 那个看守的残忍人人皆知。

items.example: He was cruelly treated as a child.
items.exampleCN: 他小时候受到残忍对待。

items.example: A cruel-hearted ruler feared no one.
items.exampleCN: 铁石心肠的统治者谁也不怕。

items.example: The cruelness of the winter surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 那个冬天的严酷让他们意外。

items.example: Crude wood must be dried first.
The crudity of his answer shocked her.
items.exampleCN: 他回答的粗鲁让她震惊。

definition_zh: 乘船游览；巡航；以稳定速度行驶
definition_en: to travel by ship for pleasure, or to move at a steady, easy speed
core_image: 白色游轮贴着蓝色海面缓缓滑过
scene: 白色游轮贴着海面缓缓滑过，甲板上的人晒着太阳。They cruise along the coast for a week each summer.
sceneCN: 这里 cruise 指「乘船游览」（第 1 个义项：为休闲而坐船航行）；句意是每年夏天他们沿着海岸巡游一周。

pos.zh: 乘船游览；巡航；以稳定速度行驶

senses.title: A pleasure voyage
senses.definition: a holiday trip by ship, or to make such a trip
senses.definitionCN: 坐船度假的旅行，或进行这样的旅行
senses.example: We took a cruise around the islands.
senses.exampleCN: 我们绕着群岛坐船玩了一圈。
senses.why: A ship turns travel itself into the destination.
senses.whyCN: 船让旅途本身变成目的地。

senses.title: Steady patrolling
senses.definition: to sail or fly on a fixed route for patrol or duty
senses.definitionCN: 沿固定路线航行或飞行以巡逻、执勤
senses.example: Two ships cruise the bay every night.
senses.exampleCN: 两艘船每晚在海湾巡航。
senses.why: A route walked again and again becomes a duty.
senses.whyCN: 同一条路线一遍遍走，就成了职责。

senses.title: A steady speed
senses.definition: to move or drive at a steady, easy speed
senses.definitionCN: 以平稳省力的速度移动或驾驶
senses.example: The car cruises at ninety on the open road.
senses.exampleCN: 这车在开阔路上以九十匀速行驶。
senses.why: At one easy speed, the machine stops fighting the road.
senses.whyCN: 保持一个省力的速度，机器就不再和路较劲。

intro.en: Cruise comes from Dutch kruisen, to cross, from Latin crux, a cross; a ship that crosses back and forth is cruising.
intro.cn: cruise 源自荷兰语 kruisen（横过、交叉），更早出自拉丁语 crux（十字）；船来回横过海面，就是巡航。

items.en: Kruisen meant to cross or move to and fro.
items.cn: kruisen 意为横过或来回移动。

items.en: It came from crux, a cross, the shape of crossing lines.
items.cn: 它出自 crux（十字），即交叉线的形状。

items.en: To cruise was to sail to and fro in search of ships.
items.cn: cruise 指在海上来回航行以搜寻船只。

items.en: Steam ships made cruising a pleasure trip.
items.cn: 汽船让巡航变成了休闲旅行。

items.en: Cars and planes now cruise at a steady speed.
items.cn: 如今汽车与飞机也以稳定速度巡航。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cru- opening and the -ise ending, and the meaning group names other journeys on water.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cru- 开头与 -ise 结尾，近义组列出其他水上旅程的说法。

entries.definition: a fast warship or a motor boat
a dark mark on the skin
a small bottle for oil or vinegar
to travel on water by wind
to move around an area to guard it

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a white ship on flat water and end with a car holding one easy speed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一艘在平静海面上的白船开始，落到一辆保持匀速的车。

normal.en: A cruise is a journey that has become the destination.
normal.cn: 乘船巡游，是旅途本身变成了目的地。

normal.en: The ship crosses the sea and calls it a holiday.
normal.cn: 船横过海面，把这叫作假期。

normal.en: Cruise control lets the car keep one steady speed.
normal.cn: 定速巡航让车保持一个稳定的速度。

normal.en: To cruise is to cross without hurry.
normal.cn: cruise 就是不慌不忙地横过去。

normal.en: A cruiser is either a warship or a fast boat.
normal.cn: cruiser 不是军舰就是快艇。

abstract.en: Picture a white ship cutting a long line in blue water.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘白船在蓝色海面上划出长线。

abstract.en: Picture a deck chair and a book left open.
abstract.cn: 想象一张甲板椅和一本摊开的书。

abstract.en: Picture a needle holding one speed on the dial.
abstract.cn: 想象指针在表盘上定住一个速度。

examples.en: They cruise the islands every winter.
examples.cn: 他们每年冬天乘船游群岛。

examples.en: The ship cruised slowly past the harbour.
examples.cn: 船缓缓驶过港口。

examples.en: He put the car in cruise and relaxed.
examples.cn: 他打开定速巡航，放松下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cruise 记成「横过去」：cru 是十字（crux），船横过海面，就成了巡游。

root: 源自荷兰语 kruisen（横过、交叉），更早出自拉丁语 crux（十字）；本义是在海面上来回横越，后指巡航，再引申为乘车船从容行进。

sensesIntro.en: From crossing the sea to patrolling it, then to any steady motion.
sensesIntro.cn: 从横越海面，到在海面巡逻，再到任何平稳的行进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white ship drawing a slow line across blue water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘白船在蓝色海面上划出缓慢的线。

branches.en: A crossing made for pleasure becomes a holiday.
branches.cn: 为享乐而做的横越，成了假期。

branches.en: A route sailed again and again becomes a patrol.
branches.cn: 一遍遍走的航线，成了巡逻。

branches.en: One easy speed is a cruise on any road.
branches.cn: 一个省力的速度，在任何路上都叫巡航。

branches.en: Pleasure trips and patrols both keep crossing the water.
branches.cn: 游船与巡逻都在不断横过水面。

branches.en: Steady motion is the thread under all three senses.
branches.cn: 平稳的行进是这三个义项共同的线。

intro.en: Cruise and cruiser belong to the Latin crux, a cross, the shape of a route that crosses water.
intro.cn: cruise 与 cruiser 属于拉丁语 crux（十字）一族，那是航线横过水面的形状。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crux, a cross, is the root under cruise and cross alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux（十字）是 cruise 与 cross 共同的根。

items.meaning: to cross water back and forth
items.example: They cruise the coast in summer.

items.meaning: a fast warship or motor boat
items.example: A cruiser met them at the bay.
items.exampleCN: 一艘巡洋舰在海湾迎接他们。

items.meaning: the act of sailing to and fro
a large ship for holiday trips
items.example: The cruise ship holds three thousand people.

items.meaning: a device that holds a steady speed
to go from one side to the other
items.example: They cross the river by ferry.

items.meaning: a long fight for a cause
items.meaningCN: 为某种主张的长久斗争
items.example: She led a crusade for clean water.
items.exampleCN: 她发起了一场争取干净水的运动。

items.example: The story says they crucified him.
items.exampleCN: 故事说他们把他钉上了十字架。

definition_zh: n. 十字军东征；运动；v. 投身运动
definition_en: a determined campaign for a cause
core_image: 人群举着旗子沿着同一条路前进
scene: 她发起了一场反对塑料垃圾的运动。She led a crusade against plastic waste.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：crusade 指运动；句意是她发起了一场反对塑料垃圾的运动。

senses.title: A cause campaign
senses.definition: a long determined effort for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 为某一事业长期坚决的努力
senses.example: The mayor began a crusade for clean air.
senses.exampleCN: 市长发起清洁空气运动。
senses.why: A crowd marching the same road.
senses.whyCN: 同一条路上行进的人群。

senses.title: A holy war
senses.definition: one of the medieval wars fought for religion
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪为宗教发动的战争
senses.example: The crusades lasted for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 十字军东征延续了数个世纪。
senses.why: A cross sewn onto a cloak.
senses.whyCN: 缝在斗篷上的十字。

senses.title: To campaign
senses.definition: to work hard in public for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某一事业奔走
senses.example: She crusaded for years against waste.
senses.exampleCN: 她为反对浪费奔走多年。
senses.why: A hand collecting signatures.
senses.whyCN: 收集签名的手。

intro.en: Crusade comes from Latin crux, cross, through cruciata, marked with a cross, and French croisade.
intro.cn: crusade 源自拉丁语 crux（十字），经 cruciata（佩十字标记的）和法语 croisade 演变。

items.en: Crux means a cross.
items.cn: crux 意为十字。

items.en: Cruciata meant marked with a cross.
items.cn: cruciata 意为佩十字的。

items.en: Croisade named the holy wars.
items.cn: croisade 指宗教战争。

items.en: Crusade named those wars in English.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 crusade 指这些战争。

items.en: Crusade named any fierce campaign.
items.cn: 十八世纪 crusade 引申为任何坚决的运动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cru- start; the near-meaning group names campaigns.
note.cn: 形近组都以 cru- 开头；近义组都是运动。

entries.definition: A group working for a shared aim.

normal.en: Today a crusade is any fierce campaign.
normal.cn: 如今 crusade 指任何坚决的运动。

normal.en: A crusade against waste is a modern example.
normal.cn: 反浪费运动就是现代例子。
